To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gallium scintigraphy is a useful tool in the diagnosis of abdominal and pelvic abscesses, and is more cost effective in this application than computed tomography and ultrasound.

(a) the sensitivity of the gallium scan is 100% and specificity is 95% for abscess; (b) the sensitivity of CT is 100% for abscess and the specificity is 100% when the CT is negative; and (c) the sensitivity of ultrasound is 100% but the specificity of ultrasound is 90% for abscess.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the detection of gallium in the presence of a large number of gallium.
the study of a new method of treatment for the prevention of postoperative adhesions, the use of a polyethylene film.
the development of a method of producing a three-dimensional (3D) image of the human body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ultrasound, CT, gallium, and angiography should all be used in the diagnosis of abscess.
the diagnostic value of ultrasound, CT, or GA67 in the diagnosis of abdominal abscess or tumor is limited and should not be relied upon as a sole diagnostic procedure.
ultrasound, CT and GA67 are complementary diagnostic modalities, which have a definite and useful place in clinical medicine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ultrasound, CT, gallium scanning, and other non-invasive diagnostic imaging procedures are valuable adjuncts to the evaluation and management of abscess and tumor.
the gallium scan is a useful adjunct to the ultrasound and CT scan.
ultrasound is the least expensive of the modalities, and it is the best method for evaluating abscesses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gallium scan is the best test for abscess, and that the gallium is the only test for abscess that can differentiate between an abscess and a tumor.
